Hi Michaël,

That will be because of the resolution of the global aerosol database I think. Which microclimate function were you using? You could also get such effects e.g. the resolution of cloud cover and rainfall.

All the best,
Mike

Thank you Mike for your reply. 

First, because I work at 1km² resolution and notably with high mountain areas, I modified the basic globalclimate.nc with regional climatic variables (1 to 4 km² of resolution) notably for cloud cover and rainfall. I just didn''t change the wind and the number of rainning days informations because I hadn't more precise data.

The global aerosol is a good idea because I used the default parameters (run.gads = 1 and TAI=0). 
Maybe is it redundant with my own cloudcover informations that include probably this informations too?

Here you can find below the function I used in the microclimate model. 
Maybe I have to change run.gads from 1 to 0 ?

Thank you very much. 

Michaël

                                             rainfrac=0,
